Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test failure and the current bug report indicate that StringUtils.join(Object[] array, char separator, int startIndex, int endIndex) throws a NullPointerException (NPE) when one of the objects in the array has a toString() method returning null.

Looking at the code of join(Object[], char, int, int):
- It returns null if the array itself is null.
- It calculates the number of items and returns an empty string if no items.
- It creates a StringBuilder buf using the length of the first element's toString() length plus 1. Specifically, it calls array[startIndex].toString().length() if array[startIndex] is not null.
- It loops through elements from startIndex to endIndex, appending separators, and appending the string representations of non-null elements (array[i] != null).

The key issue lies in this line:
```java
StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder((array[startIndex] == null ? 16 : array[startIndex].toString().length()) + 1);
```
Here, if array[startIndex] is not null, it calls array[startIndex].toString().length() directly without checking if the toString() returns null. If toString() returns null, calling length() on it causes a NullPointerException.

Similarly, the appending loop:
```java
if (array[i] != null) {
    buf.append(array[i]);
}
```
The append(Object) method in StringBuilder internally calls String.valueOf(obj), which safely converts null to "null" string, so this part should not cause NPE.

Therefore, the root cause is specifically the initial buffer size estimation line accessing array[startIndex].toString().length() without checking if toString() is null.

Recent bug reports do not mention this issue directly, so they provide no additional useful information.

Hence, the bug is caused by the assumption that the toString method of the array's first element is non-null, which is incorrect per the current bug report.

This leads to the NPE on calling length() on a null string returned by toString().

The test failure with testJoin_ArrayChar likely triggers this by passing an object whose toString() returns null.

Conclusion: The bug lies in the join method in StringUtils at the buffer size initialization line, which does not safely handle null from toString().

Next, I will identify methods to fix.
StringUtils.join(java.lang.Object[],char,int,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
